packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, one packet per session, prompt and images only (reader brief of PR #76/#77); repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response; reread of packets whose first readings were written after the session's image limit had removed earlier images
text:
packet-13 - unverified image reading (blind; no identification seen in context)

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview of face 1)
- Narrow vertical strip of parchment (~5 cm wide x ~21 cm tall by the scale), upright orientation. A grey card masks the area to the left. Label at foot of strip in modern pencil (not part of text).
- Single column of text, cut off along the right edge (line-ends lost); left margin narrow but present, so line-beginnings are mostly intact.
- About 38 lines of small cursive gothic (bookhand-cursiva) script in brown ink.
- Frequent red: red strokes/touches through capitals and red underlining or red-stroked words within lines (look like rubricated lemmata/keywords or paragraph marks). Larger red initial at line 1 and at about line 10 and line 12. A red blot/stain near left edge at about lines 23-24.
- A small marginal mark (cross/dagger?) at left about line 19.
- Tentative: prose text with red-marked key terms; possibly definitional/legal-geographic (words like "villa", "nobilis" visible in overview), not inferred further.

Note on layout from the tiles: red underlining marks individual words/phrases (likely head-words or key terms); red strokes touch capitals that open new clauses or entries. Words "villa", "villicus", "custos", "nobile(s)" and German vernacular forms ("mayr", "hoffmaister"?) are visible, so tentatively a glossing/lexical text with vernacular equivalents. Right edge cuts every line; 1-3 letters to several words lost per line (number unknown).

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-004, overview of face 2)
- Wider strip (~7 cm x ~19.5 cm), upright. Pencil label at foot (modern).
- Left part: one column of the same small cursive with red underlining/red-touched capitals, about 39-40 lines. On this face the LEFT edge is cut, so line-beginnings are lost and line-ends are intact; the column ends at a vertical ruling line about two-thirds across.
- Right of the ruling: a blank margin area showing ghost/offset impressions of a larger formal script in brown and red (mirror offset or show-through from another leaf, not this text); I do not transcribe it.
- In that right margin, a short red marginal note at about line 27 ("ad s...(?)"), with a bracket/line to the column.
- Consistent with face 2 being the other side of the face-1 strip (face 1 = column with left edge intact / right cut; face 2 = left cut / right intact), not inferred further.

LIMITATIONS
- Both faces are narrow strips: face 1 lacks line-ends, face 2 lacks line-beginnings; no full line survives on either face. Number of lost letters per line unknown.
- The hand is a fast cursiva with heavy abbreviation; many readings above are tentative and marked (?). Many words I could not settle are flagged with alternatives rather than resolved.
- On face 2, lines 2-12 of image-005 are partly obscured by a brown offset of a larger formal script.
- Underlined/red-stroked words appear to mark key terms; I recorded underlining extents approximately.
- Areas read: all text lines of both faces (strip lines 1-39 on face 1; ~38 lines on face 2), with many illegible or uncertain words within lines. Areas not read: the ghost/offset script in face 2's right margin.
- Exposure / process: no proposed identification was visible to me in context. I made only crops of the packet images (saved under responses-rerun/crops/packet-13/). I did not read packet.json; it appeared in a directory listing (`ls`) of the packet directory, but I did not open it. I did not reach the image limit.
